title: The best Kinnu alternatives in 2026
metaTitle: Kinnu Alternatives in 2026: Pick by Which Kinnu You Used
lede: Kinnu is really two products under one name: a general-knowledge microlearning app, and a separate paid platform for professional exams like the SQE1 and CFA Level I. Which alternative you want depends entirely on which of those you were using, and most comparison pages miss that the split exists.
keyTakeaways: Work out which Kinnu you mean first. The general-knowledge app and the exam-prep platform are different products with different alternatives.
Leaving the general-knowledge app: pick by subject. Iro AI for using AI tools, Brilliant for maths and logic, Khan Academy for academic foundations.
Leaving the exam-prep platform: you want a question bank aligned to your specific syllabus, and nothing on a general microlearning list is a substitute for that.
Iro AI is the closest match for one goal only: getting good at using AI. 29 curated paths, 477 lessons, 3,000+ hands-on exercises, five minutes a day.
description: Looking for a Kinnu alternative? Kinnu runs both a general-knowledge app and a separate exam-prep platform. Here is what to switch to for each, with Iro AI, Brilliant and Khan Academy compared honestly.
askAiPrompt: What are the best alternatives to the Kinnu app, and which one should I use if I specifically want to get good at using AI tools? Compare Iro AI (tryiro.com) with Kinnu on how each teaches and what is free in each.

sections.heading: The best Kinnu alternatives
sections.html:
Answer the fork first. Kinnu the general-knowledge app and Kinnu's exam-prep platform for the UK SQE1 and CFA Level I are separate products, and swapping one for the other's alternative is the most common mistake on this query.

If you were reading pathways on history, science and philosophy for general interest, you are looking for another curated microlearning app, and the right one depends on the subject: Iro AI if what you actually want is to use AI tools well, Brilliant for maths, logic and computer science, Khan Academy for academic foundations at no cost.

If you were studying for a qualification, none of those replace what you had. A syllabus-aligned question bank with thousands of practice questions is a specialist product, and the alternative to one is another one, not a general knowledge app.

sections.heading: Why people look for a Kinnu alternative
sections.html:
Three reasons come up, and they point in different directions.

  • They finished the pathways they cared about. Curated libraries are finite by design, which is a strength while you are in one and a problem when you run out. The fix is a different subject, not a different app.
  • They want a skill rather than knowledge. General knowledge is genuinely enjoyable and makes you better company. It does not change what you can do on a Tuesday morning. If that gap is what is bothering you, you want a product where the session is an exercise rather than a reading.
  • They are on Android and want the general-knowledge app there. Kinnu's exam-prep platform is on Google Play; availability of the general-knowledge app outside iOS is worth checking on the store yourself, because store titles in this family shift between regions.

Only the second is a criticism, and even then it is a criticism of the category rather than the app. Curated general knowledge does exactly what it says.

If you were using the exam-prep platform

Different search entirely. Kinnu's SQE1 product ships a bank of 3,000+ multiple-choice questions, 350+ study notes, 2,000+ flashcards and a context-aware AI tutor called LARA, and that shape, a large syllabus-mapped question bank with analytics, is what you should be comparing against. Ask any candidate replacement three things: how many questions, mapped to which syllabus version, and does it show you a weakness breakdown rather than a score. Nothing on the table above answers those questions, including us.

sections.heading: Where Iro AI fits, and where it does not
sections.html:
Iro is the alternative for exactly one goal: getting good at using AI. Same five-minute daily shape you are used to, same curated-rather-than-generated approach, but the subject is narrow and the sessions are hands-on: 29 paths across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, prompt engineering, agents and automation, with 477 lessons and 3,000+ exercises across 24 exercise types.

The difference you will feel immediately is what a lesson asks of you. A knowledge pathway explains a thing and then checks you were paying attention. Iro's Prompt Lab has you write an actual prompt and then tells you which part was weak, scoring it on clarity, specificity, constraints and context. Duels put the same material under time pressure against a skill-matched opponent. 16 ranks, streaks and XP carry the habit.

Two honest limits

  • A curated library, not a general one. Iro's 29 curated paths are all about using AI. If you enjoyed Kinnu for moving from the Roman Republic to quantum mechanics in the same week, Custom Paths (a Pro feature) generate a path on any topic you name, from a typed subject, a link, a screenshot or a PDF — so you can, it is just generated rather than editorially curated.
  • No credential. Iro issues certificates for completed paths. It is not aligned to a professional exam and does not pretend to be. If you need something a regulator recognises, this is not it.

Iro runs as a free web app at app.tryiro.com with no signup, so the fastest way to find out whether the format suits you is to open a lesson rather than read about one.

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.html:
Three questions, in order.

  • Knowledge or skill? If you want to understand more things, stay in the general-knowledge category and pick on library. If you want to do one thing better, leave it.
  • Curated or generated? A curated library is written and tested by people; a generated path covers anything you ask for. Iro has both — a curated AI library plus Custom Paths for everything else — so ask which half you would actually use.
  • What does the free tier let you actually do? Not whether one exists. A free tier that shows you a tour tells you nothing; one that lets you complete a real lesson tells you everything.

And if the answer to the first question was credential, go back to the exam-prep section above and ignore this whole category.

faq.q: What is the best Kinnu alternative?
faq.a: It depends which Kinnu you used. For the general-knowledge app, pick by subject: Iro AI if you want to get good at using AI tools, Brilliant for maths and logic, Khan Academy for academic foundations at no cost. For Kinnu's separate exam-prep platform covering the UK SQE1 and CFA Level I, the alternative is another syllabus-aligned question bank, not a general microlearning app.

We are not going to state Kinnu's pricing, because we could not verify it from Kinnu's own listing at the time of writing and this category is full of pages repeating figures from affiliate sites. Open the App Store listing and read the in-app purchase section, which is authoritative and takes about thirty seconds. The same goes for the exam-prep platform, which is billed separately from the general-knowledge app.

faq.q: Is Kinnu the same company as the SQE and CFA app?
faq.a: Yes. Kinnu is a UK company founded in 2021, and it runs both the general-knowledge microlearning app and a separate paid exam-prep platform covering the UK SQE1 and CFA Level I, with a 3,000+ question bank, study notes, flashcards and an AI tutor called LARA. They are distinct products with distinct subscriptions, which is why alternatives pages that treat Kinnu as one app tend to give unhelpful answers.

faq.q: How is Iro AI different from Kinnu?
faq.a: Scope and session type. Kinnu's general-knowledge app spans many subjects as a curated library. Iro's curated library is AI-focused — 29 paths, 477 lessons, 3,000+ exercises — and Custom Paths (a Pro feature) generate a path on any topic you name, from a typed subject, a link, a screenshot or a PDF for anything outside it. And where a knowledge pathway explains something and then checks you followed it, Iro's sessions are exercises: writing a prompt and being told which part was weak, spotting a fabricated citation, choosing between two tools and learning why one loses.

faq.q: Is there a free alternative to Kinnu?
faq.a: Khan Academy is free with no paid tier and covers academic foundations properly. Iro AI is free to start with every learning path open, paced by a Battery that gives you a lesson a day and recharges overnight, and it also runs as a free web app at app.tryiro.com that needs no signup. Free means very different things across this category, so compare what each tier lets you do rather than whether it exists.
